description: tags(span) of a span that is not a whole capture reads the tokens of the projected span. The chosen a restores T before A, B and C, so R is T A T B T C. tail($) projects to B C, so its tags are B and C, and a survives beside c, which reads each T as a bare terminal. A library that takes the union over the tokens of R behind tail($), from the original B to the original C, takes in the synthetic T between them, loses a, and passes (engine §7.5).
grammar:
%ambiguity-resolution late-elision elision-only
%elidable T
%rule text a | b | c
%rule a [T] A [T] B [T] C
%conditions tags(tail($)) = B ∪ C
%rule b [T] [T] A [T] [T] B [T] [T] C
%rule c T A T B T C
